candidate.rationale: The function returns unit; its only modeled effect is consuming the linear PointsTo token. Public vstd vocabulary exposes no allocator-liveness predicate, so deallocation cannot be stated as a useful postcondition.
risks: Memory invalidation is represented only by linear permission consumption; the copied PPtr value itself remains available.

candidate.rationale: The meaningful effect is consumption of the linear PointsTo token, which is enforced by tracked ownership rather than represented as a post-state predicate. The function returns unit and exposes no allocator state or liveness predicate, so any expressible ensures would only restate a precondition or be vacuous.
risks: Adding true, a unit-result property, or perm.pptr() == self would not characterize deallocation.
The copied PPtr value remains available, but cannot be used safely without a corresponding PointsTo token.
